name: Update Score
desc: Updates a single scoreboard entry (add, remove, or change score value).

writeup.p: Single-row scoreboard mutation. Fields are the score name (40-char cap), an action enum (CHANGE or REMOVE), the objective name (16-char cap), and for CHANGE a VarInt value. The server emits one S3C per row update: value change, row removal, removal scoped to one objective, and full replay during objective creation and on join. It is the most frequently emitted scoreboard packet: a 15-row sidebar refresh is 15 packets.

handleUpdateScore resolves the objective by name, then either sets the score points (CHANGE) or removes the row (REMOVE). A REMOVE with an empty objective name removes the row from every objective. The client scoreboard then re-renders whichever slot binds the objective. The value field is only present for CHANGE, so the read path is action-dependent.

Two Spicy files rewrite this packet, both for name visibility. HideName replaces the session username with a chosen alias in both the objective name and the row name fields, so sidebar kill feeds and stats boards stop showing the real name. Account.java does the inverse for alt accounts: it appends the real account name in green so the user can tell which identity is live. Both mutate the decoded packet inside EventPacket pre, before the vanilla handler runs. Rise 6.x only registers the class in the script API.

Name rewriting here is invisible to the server: S3C is clientbound, and the rewrite happens after decode and before the client scoreboard consumes it. Anti-cheats never see the mutation. HideName stays consistent by applying the same alias to chat (S02PacketChat) and scoreboard rows, so the client-side story matches everywhere. There is no server-side state to desync because the scoreboard lives only on the client.

implementation.overview: The only scoreboard packet the 8 clients actually mutate. Spicy's HideName swaps the player's username for an alias in score rows; Spicy's Account.java appends the real alt name in green. Both rewrite the decoded packet before the vanilla handler, which the server cannot see.
implementation.server_handling: ServerScoreboard emits S3C on score value changes, row removal, and removal scoped to one objective, plus full replays during objective creation and join. All sends go through sendPacketToAllPlayers. The packet is clientbound only; the server never validates or receives score state back from the client.
implementation.protocol_notes: readPacketData order: score name (40-char cap), action enum via readEnumValue, objective name (16-char cap), then the VarInt value only when the action is CHANGE. REMOVE rows omit the value, keeping the packet short. The enum has exactly two members, CHANGE and REMOVE; there is no separate add action.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Nothing flags S3C abuse in the corpus. It carries display strings and a display integer, no timing or movement content. Rewriting name fields is purely cosmetic client-side work that server-side anti-cheat cannot detect.

modules.name: HideName
modules.purpose: Stop the player's real username from appearing in scoreboard rows: sidebar stats, kill feeds, and per-player objectives.
modules.how_it_works: In EventPacket pre, when the packet is S3CPacketUpdateScore, it strips the invisible joiner character (׼) from both name fields and checks whether the objective name or the score name contains the session username. On a match it replaces the username with the selected alias via setObjective and setName. The same handler rewrites S02PacketChat for chat surfaces.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: None. Pure client-side string rewrite after decode; the server never sees the mutation.
modules.variations: Account.java reuses the same rewrite pattern but appends the real account name in green instead of hiding it.

modules.name: Account (alt name reveal)
modules.purpose: For alt accounts, append the real account name to the player's own scoreboard rows so the user can tell which identity is live.
modules.how_it_works: Account.onPacket, reached from the module event bus when SpicyClient.account.loggedIn is true, handles S3CPacketUpdateScore by rewriting the objective name and row name, replacing the session username with 'username §f(§a realname §f)'. The same treatment applies to S02PacketChat. It also polls the SpicyClient.info API per player to map alt names to real accounts.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: None. The rewrite is client-side after decode; the server only ever sent the alt username.
modules.variations: HideName performs the same two-field rewrite with a fake name; Account.java uses the real account name from the login session.

modules.name: NetworkAPI (script API)
modules.purpose: Expose the packet class to Rise's JavaScript scripting API so scripts can construct, read, or match it.
modules.how_it_works: S3CPacketUpdateScore is listed in the clientbound Class array of NetworkAPI.java (line 103). Scripts use the table to instantiate or filter the packet.
modules.variations: 6.2.4 ships the byte-identical file with the Client-release2 path prefix.

implementation.general_hooks: Spicy: EventPacket pre on the client event bus. Rise 6.x: script API table.
implementation.client_variations: Spicy mutates the packet object in place (setObjective/setName). Rise 6.x has no module code for this packet, only the script registry.

anticheat.overview: S3C is the single-row scoreboard mutation, and no anticheat flags it. The only live consumer is Shard's monitor, which renders its status sidebar by emitting the scoreboard family itself, including the S3C row updates. The rest of the corpus is registrations (Negativity PacketType SCOREBOARD_SCORE, Artemis PacketRepository SERVER_PLAY+57 with the PacketPlayServerScoreboardScore wrapper and HardcodeMap) and keyword noise: intave's hits handle the sibling S3E team packet and matched on the Scoreboard search term, NCP's CollisionUtil reads the Bukkit scoreboard API for team collision predicates, and amnoah's ReloadCommand mentions BetterScoreboard in a comment.

checks.name: Monitor sidebar bridge (Shard)
checks.purpose: The anticheat's own scoreboard HUD: Shard renders its monitor sidebar by sending the client the scoreboard packets itself, including the S3C row updates.
checks.how_it_works: ScoreboardPacketBridge constructs and sends the full scoreboard family to a viewer: WrapperPlayServerScoreboardObjective for the objective (adventure-component title on 1.20.3+ with a legacy fallback), WrapperPlayServerDisplayScoreboard for the slot binding, and WrapperPlayServerUpdateScore for each row, with CREATE_OR_UPDATE_ITEM carrying the score value and REMOVE_ITEM handling deletions on servers below 1.20.3 (WrapperPlayServerResetScore replaces the remove path on 1.20.3+). updateEntry is the S3C producer: one packet per sidebar row per refresh.
checks.detects: Nothing cheat-related. It is the anticheat as scoreboard producer; keeping the monitor readable is a HUD concern, not a flag.
checks.variations: The rest of the corpus does not read S3C. Negativity and Artemis only register the packet class (SCOREBOARD_SCORE constant, SERVER_PLAY+57 repository entry, wrapper interface); intave's EntityCollisionDisabler and ScoreboardAccessor handle the sibling S3E team packet, matched here only by the Scoreboard keyword.

checks.name: TextComponentScore emulator render (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Render chat score components inside the world emulator by substituting the score value for a named objective and entry.
checks.how_it_works: TextComponentScore is the moderna text-component subclass behind the score placeholder. Its resolve path looks up the objective on the emulated world's Bukkit scoreboard and writes score.getScorePoints() into the value (lines 61-77), and getUnformattedComponentText returns that value. The scoreboard lookup is inside a resolve() method that is commented out in the cloned source, so the class never queries the scoreboard at runtime. The corpus hit is the Scoreboard keyword, not the packet: Artemis reads score state through the server API and never parses S3C.
checks.detects: Nothing. Score text in the emulated chat pipeline only; the renderer substitutes what the server scoreboard already holds, and in the clone even that path is disabled.
checks.variations: None. Artemis's PacketPlayServerScoreboardScore, PacketPlayServerScoreboardObjective, PacketPlayServerScoreboardObjectiveDisplay and PacketPlayServerScoreboardTeam interfaces are repository wrappers only.
